name: Biometric authentication
plain: Lets the app ask the system to verify the user with fingerprint or face.
meaning: The app never sees the biometric; it gets a pass or fail. Face ID needs a purpose string.

ios.prompt_ui: Face ID permission prompt on first use
ios.revocation: Settings > Face ID & Passcode > Other apps
ios.note: Touch ID needs no purpose string; Face ID does.

limits.headline: Can ask the phone to check your fingerprint or face, without seeing either
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in, Approve payment, or Unlock and use your fingerprint or face
can: Show the system fingerprint or face prompt
Learn a yes or no answer after the check
Fall back to your PIN or passcode if you choose that
Unlock a stored secret after a successful check
cannot: See your fingerprint, face map or the scan itself
Run the check silently without showing the prompt
Get a yes when the scan fails and you did not use your passcode
Learn which finger or face matched
limits.reach_label: A yes or no from the phone
limits.differs: iPhone needs a Face ID purpose message; Touch ID does not. Android shows a standard BiometricPrompt.

story.what_it_is: An app asks the phone to confirm it is you using a face or fingerprint scan.

marketing.name: Face ID and Touch ID
marketing.pitch: Unlock, sign in and pay securely with your face or fingerprint.

marketing.name: Biometric authentication
marketing.pitch: Android shows a standard prompt so apps can use fingerprint or face to confirm you.

story.for_you: You see a standard system prompt asking for your face or fingerprint. You scan and the app gets only yes or no. The app never sees your face or print.
story.for_makers: Makers get strong proof that the right person is holding the phone, without storing biometric data. It speeds up logins and payments. It also lets them guard sensitive screens like balances or messages.

use_cases.example: You open your bank app and unlock it with Face ID instead of typing a 6 digit code.
You approve a payment in a shop or delivery app with one fingerprint touch.
Your notes app locks private notes and opens them with your face.
A secure chat app asks for biometrics when you open it, so a borrowed phone cannot read your chats.
A game store asks for a fingerprint before it confirms a purchase, which protects kids' accounts.
A health app protects test results behind a scan.

risks: Face unlock may be forced by others
story.android_note: Android offers weak and strong biometrics, and apps pick which level they need.
story.ios_note: iPhone requires a short purpose text for Face ID so the app can say why it asks.

technical_bounds: Biometry changes can invalidate bound keys
No raw biometric data crosses the app boundary
